intro: Step into Sivrihisar Great Mosque, a mosque and complex in Eskişehir province, built in 1274. Look around you: sixty-seven wooden columns carry the roof, more than in any other Anatolian hypostyle mosque, and some of their capitals were reused from ancient buildings.
history: The mosque was built in 1274. Its flat roof rests on sixty-seven wooden columns, making it the most heavily columned timber mosque in Anatolia. Look closely at the capitals: some were reused from ancient buildings. It entered the World Heritage List in 2023, together with the other wooden hypostyle mosques.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the sixty-seven columns and their reused capitals. Pause at the wooden minbar, and look up at the beamed ceiling.
facts: Did you know? The joints were left deliberately loose, so that the timber could take up and give off moisture without splitting the frame. And with sixty-seven wooden columns, this is the most heavily columned timber mosque in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our tour of Sivrihisar Great Mosque to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This timber forest has stood for centuries; let it keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
